early blight.description: Early blight appears as small brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, causing premature defoliation.
treatment: Spray fungicides like mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or azoxystrobin at early symptoms.
prevention: Avoid overhead irrigation and ensure good field sanitation.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150–180 kg Nitrogen, 80–100 kg Phosphorus, and 120–150 kg Potassium per hectare.
Use adequate potassium for disease resistance.
soil_recommendation: Prefer sandy loam to loam soils with good drainage.
Avoid soil compaction to reduce stress.

healthy.description: Healthy potato plants have green leaves, strong stems, and produce tubers without disease symptoms.
treatment: Conduct regular monitoring for early disease detection.
prevention: Use certified seeds and resistant varieties.
Rotate crops and maintain field hygiene.
Apply preventive fungicides if nearby fields show infection.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150–180 kg Nitrogen, 80–100 kg Phosphorus, and 120–150 kg Potassium per hectare.
Split nitrogen applications during growth stages.
soil_recommendation: Maintain organic matter for better soil health.

late blight.description: Late blight causes water-soaked lesions on leaves and stems, turning black. Tubers develop dark, sunken, firm rot.
treatment: Spray systemic fungicides (metalaxyl, cymoxanil, dimethomorph) combined with protectants (mancozeb, chlorothalonil).
Destroy heavily infected plants to limit spread.
prevention: Ensure proper plant spacing for good aeration.
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness by managing irrigation.
fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 150–200 kg Nitrogen, 80–100 kg Phosphorus, and 120–150 kg Potassium per hectare.
Higher potassium improves tolerance to late blight.
soil_recommendation: Avoid excess irrigation to reduce humidity.
